messages:
alex: @channel automated alerts — we’re seeing a sudden drop in Datadog APM/span ingestion and a backlog on metric ingestion across eu-west-1. UI shows gaps starting ~09:07 UTC. Paging oncall now.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: #DB-OBS-17678 — High-level symptom: Datadog ingestion delays causing partial observability. Pager duty notified.

pagerduty-bot: Paging maya (oncall) and ryan (secondary).

maya: I’m on it, grabbing logs for the dd-agent and forwarding queues. Seeing a bunch of WARNs about rate-limits and 'ingester backlog' in host dd-agg-03.

ryan: Confirmed — top-level latency alerts are real, but our internal emitter shows normal egress to Datadog endpoint. Could be ingestion side. Any Datadog status?

datadog-status-bot: Datadog status: https://status.datadoghq.com/ — current incidents: "Ingestion delays in EU regions" (updated 09:15 UTC).

alex: Good — looks like third-party. We still need to mitigate customer impact and restore as much visibility as possible. Quick checklist: 1) Turn on local buffering for metrics, 2) Redirect critical metrics/traces to our S3 archival + offline processor, 3) Enable fallback dashboards from ingestion logs.

maya: Working through #1 now. On dd-agg-03:
```
sudo systemctl restart datadog-agent
journalctl -u datadog-agent -n 200 | tail -n 80
# seeing: "Forwarder error: 429 Too Many Requests" and "backlog size: 12433 events"
```
\nryan: For #2, I’ll flip the emitter to write critical traces/metrics to s3://redwood-backups/datadog-proxy/ to avoid data loss. Doing a quick sim and will keep copies for replay.

support-lead: Heads-up: support queue already has 3 customers asking about missing infra metrics in dashboards. Drafting a status message: "Partial observability: performance dashboards delayed — no customer data loss anticipated; metrics will replay once third-party clears backlog." Any objections?

alex: Sounds good. Add note to avoid promising timelines. Mention we're monitoring and will update hourly.

maya: quick mitigation step applied — increased dd-agent forwarder buffer and enabled local file spool on dd-agg-*. That should reduce dropped events while Datadog recovers.

ryan: I’ve kicked off the s3 writer and tagged today's objects with incident id DB-OBS-17678. Uploads in progress (~2.3 MB/s).

maya: Additional note — our other observability paths (internal prometheus scrape + synthetic checks) still working. I pushed a temporary dashboard that uses prometheus metrics for latency/throughput so ops can triage without Datadog. Link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/incident-17678

support-lead: Posting incident update to status.redwood.com: "Third-party ingestion delays affecting visibility. We are mitigating and providing fallback dashboards. No customer request failures identified at this time." Posting now.

alex: Can someone open a support ticket with Datadog and push for an ETA? We need to escalate to severity. Include our queue sizes and host samples.

maya: Ticket created: DD-TICKET-94231. I included: backlog counts, sample host logs, and timestamps. Datadog response: "Investigating ingestion backlog in EU-West; no ETA yet."

datadog-status-bot: Update from Datadog (09:37 UTC): "We are experiencing sustained ingestion delays in some EU clusters. Engineers are working. Backlogs are being processed; customers may see delayed data for up to several hours."

ryan: Ok. Plan B for triage: enable short-term local aggregations and synthetic alerting to catch customer-facing errors (4xx/5xx spikes). I’ll drop alerts to Slack + PagerDuty for user-impacting thresholds so we don’t rely on Datadog.

alex: Agree. Also run a quick audit of rate-limit config — want to ensure our agents aren’t being throttled due to batching config changes earlier this week.

maya: Found a mis-tuned batch window on dd-agg-02 (batch size 50 -> causing spikes). I reverted to batch size 10 and restarted forwarders. Backlog delta decreasing on that host from 12k -> 9k in last 10m.

support-lead: Support update pushed to customers (09:52 UTC): "We are aware of delayed performance metrics due to Datadog ingestion issues. Engineers are mitigating; dashboards updated to use fallback metrics where available." Small set of customers asked for confirmation of no data loss — we reiterated that we're replaying raw events to Datadog once their ingestion clears.

maya: New Datadog PR update (10:04 UTC): "Backlogs processing; ingestion rates returning toward normal. Some customers will see delayed data as backfill occurs."

alex: Good sign. Keep watch on our SLO breakouts and on-call queue. If Datadog clears backlog, watch for backfill spikes that could confuse alerting — add suppression window: 15m for metric bursts from backfill.

ryan: Implemented suppression: alert_rules/temporary_suppress.json updated and pushed. Also added note in incident to ignore transient spike alerts coming from datadog-backfill tag.

maya: Handing over to night oncall — @ryan you’ll be lead for the rest of the window. I’ll summarize everything in the incident doc and hand off.

ryan: Oncall ack. I’ll monitor Datadog status, S3 replay completion, and watch for customer-impacting alerts.

datadog-status-bot: (10:28 UTC) Datadog update: "Processing backlog; ingestion throughput improving. Customers should see metrics repopulate over next 1-3 hours."

support-lead: We logged 7 support tickets about missing dashboards. 2 customers flagged higher latencies in their apps, but tracing was available via our fallback path and we confirmed downstream services OK. Communicating individually.

alex: Thanks team. Once Datadog confirms cleared backlog, we’ll remove suppression and close incident. If backlog persists beyond 4 hours escalate with our account manager.

datadog-status-bot: (12:05 UTC) FINAL: "Backlog cleared in EU-West clusters, ingestion normalized. If you still observe gaps, open a support ticket with payload samples."

maya: Verified incoming metrics/traces repopulating in Datadog UI for the affected window. No lost events reported; replay succeeded for archived objects.

ryan: Removing suppression window and re-enabling normal alerting rules.

alex: Incident resolved — marking as resolved in our tracker. Follow-up actions: 1) postmortem to cover hardening forwarder batching defaults and DR replay automation, 2) contact Datadog AM about SLA/credits, 3) add automatic fallback dashboard to status page.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: DB-OBS-17678 — Resolution: Datadog backlog cleared and visibility restored.

support-lead: Final support update posted to customers. Closing support tickets where appropriate. :white_check_mark:

alex: Thanks everyone — nice run.
